issues.evidence: I counted them one at a time, left to right, in the right third of the frame: (1) the leftmost, nearest the horse's head, leafy crown highest; (2) the next to its right; (3) the third; (4) the rightmost, crown lowest. Each has its own unbroken shaft running down into the shallow water and its own separate reflection below it. There is no fifth shaft anywhere in the row. I re-opened the image specifically to recount and got four both times. The rider's ornate gold staff with the ring finial and star is a fifth pole-like object, but it is visually distinct in form, material and placement, and the existing text already lists it separately as its own keyObject — so it cannot be what the row of 'five' refers to.
